title: Grade 4 Math — Fri, Jun 20
description: Geometry — Day 5 of 5: Mixed review — lines, angles, and triangles
subject: mathematics

questions.question: Lines that never meet and are always the same distance apart are called:
questions.explanation: Parallel lines never intersect and are equidistant. E.g. railway tracks.

questions.question: Lines that meet at exactly 90° are:
questions.explanation: Perpendicular lines meet at right angles (90°).

questions.question: An angle of 75° is classified as:
An angle of 165° is classified as:
An angle of 300° is classified as:
A triangle with all sides 6 cm and all angles 60° is:
questions.explanation: All sides equal, all angles 60° → equilateral triangle.

questions.question: A triangle with sides 5 cm, 8 cm, and 5 cm and angles 50°, 80°, 50° is:
questions.explanation: Two equal sides (5 cm) and two equal angles (50°) → isosceles triangle.

questions.question: In a right triangle, the two non-right angles must sum to:
questions.explanation: Right angle = 90°. Remaining angles = 180° − 90° = 90°. So the other two angles sum to 90°.

questions.question: The letter 'X' is formed by two straight lines. What type of lines are these?
questions.explanation: The two lines in 'X' cross each other but not at 90° — they are intersecting lines (not perpendicular).

questions.question: A square has how many pairs of parallel sides?
questions.explanation: A square has 2 pairs of parallel sides: top and bottom parallel, left and right parallel.

questions.question: Find the missing angle: A triangle has angles 55° and 85°. The third angle is:
A triangle with angles 100°, 40°, and 40° is classified as:
questions.explanation: One angle > 90° (100°) → obtuse. Two equal angles (40° = 40°) → isosceles. So: obtuse isosceles.

questions.question: How many right angles does a regular clock face have from 12 to 3, 3 to 6, 6 to 9, 9 to 12?
questions.explanation: Each quarter turn (12→3, 3→6, 6→9, 9→12) is 90°. Four such turns = 4 right angles = 360°.

questions.question: Which of the following shapes has NO right angles?
questions.explanation: Equilateral triangle has all angles = 60° (acute). No right angles. Squares, rectangles, and right triangles all have 90° angles.

questions.question: WEEK STAR: A triangle has one angle that is a right angle and the other two angles are equal. What are the other two angles?
questions.explanation: Right angle = 90°. Remaining = 180° − 90° = 90°. Split equally: 90° ÷ 2 = 45° each. This is a right isosceles triangle.
